comment: Task 81 (census-as-gate): per-demo REQUIRED registered script members. result_schema.py
fails a run whose exercisedMembers census is missing any 'required' member, naming it.
Member spelling is 'ClassSuffix.memberName', suffix-matched against the census's fully
qualified script class names; memberName is the Godot-facing name from the export's
Scope: the census records DISPATCHES ACROSS THE JS<->Kotlin BOUNDARY -- exactly the
surface where the Web dispatch-degradation class of bugs lives (the FPS Enemy.damage
break was a missing dispatch arm). A member invoked Kotlin-to-Kotlin (e.g. via
kotlinScriptInstance) never crosses and CANNOT be required here; such members appear as
'todo' rows with the transitive evidence that covers them. 'todo' rows are honesty
markers, never enforced -- a gap must be visible, not silently omitted.
An absent demo or an empty 'required' list passes (ratchet: tighten as drivers grow).
Every list below was confirmed against a measured envelope before being required.

required.reason: The Area3D overlap that starts the scoring chain; the driver pins the player onto the coin (KANAMA_WEB_T81_FALSIFY=no-coin suppresses exactly this).
The scene-wired coin_collected handler updating the Coins label; its only emitter is Player.collectCoin, so this transitively proves the Kotlin-side collect ran.

todo.reason: Called Kotlin-to-Kotlin (Coin.onBodyEntered resolves the Player via kotlinScriptInstance), so it never crosses the recorded dispatch boundary; covered transitively by Hud._on_coin_collected above.

required.reason: MobTimer-driven spawning; without it no mob exists and every other squash assertion is vacuous.
The squashed-signal scoring handler; its only emitter is Mob.squash, so this transitively proves the Kotlin-side squash ran (KANAMA_WEB_T81_FALSIFY=no-chase suppresses the choreography).
The lose path: a mob reaching the MobDetector kills the player (KANAMA_WEB_T81_FALSIFY=no-death suppresses the ground park that allows it).
The scene-wired hit handler that stops the MobTimer and shows Retry -- the lose path's consequence, one signal downstream of Player.die.

todo.reason: Called Kotlin-to-Kotlin (Player resolves the Mob via kotlinScriptInstance), so it never crosses the recorded dispatch boundary; covered transitively by ScoreLabel._on_Mob_squashed above.

required.reason: The member whose silent dispatch death started task 81: Player's shot reaches the enemy proxy's damage(amount: float) and crosses via callDoubles (task 79/80). Enemies were immortal on Web for weeks while every gate stayed green.
Enemy return fire: the RayCast attack tick that makes the firefight two-sided runs on a scene Timer every run.

todo.reason: Ranked gap #4 (task 81): on Web the enemy resolves the Player via kotlinScriptInstance and calls damage Kotlin-to-Kotlin, so the census cannot see it, and no driver asserts the health HUD chain (_on_health_updated) yet.

required.reason: The driver adds 256 bunnies through this member; the demo's population depends on it.
The driver removes a bunny to advance a handle generation for the stale-handle proof.
The driver's teardown entry: frees the bunnies and reports the final counts.
The driver starts (and later restarts) the round through this member -- the demo's whole lifecycle hangs off it.
Mob spawning; without it the mobsSpawnAndFree evidence is vacuous.
The round's start delay elapsing is what arms the mob and score timers.

todo.reason: Host-variant lifecycle (task 71: mobs never free on Linux Firefox, cell quarantined). The required-member gate has no per-engine quarantine mechanism, so requiring this would re-litigate the quarantine at the schema layer; the driver's mobsSpawnAndFree check carries it where it holds.
Fires only when a mob happens to hit the stationary player -- nondeterministic inside the smoke window. Driving the game-over transition is ranked gap #5 in the task-81 spec.

required.reason: The driver's synthetic pointer press lands on a board tile; every match/collapse/refill assertion begins here.
The tile press reaching Main's board logic -- the match pipeline's entry.
The tween-completion handler for tile movement: collapse/refill actually finished moving tiles, not merely started.

todo.reason: Fires when a sound effect ENDS, which races the driver's window; requiring it would gate on timing, not gameplay.

required.reason: Every build/demolish/rotate/save/load action is handled inside Builder's _process input polling -- the demo registers no gameplay methods at all, so this virtual is the only member-level evidence; the driver's GridMap content checks remain the substantive gameplay gate.

todo.reason: Placement sounds end asynchronously; requiring it would gate on timing. The demo's registered-member surface is otherwise empty (2 members total in the census table).

The web3d fixture is probe-driven (generic-callv and render probes); its member-level requirements should be written when the probe surface stabilizes -- today the driver's own probe checks are the gate.

The driver holds drive input and asserts View movement; beyond the Smoke teardown entry no registered method is exercised (spec table: 3 of 5 members never invoked). Needs driver work, not a list entry.

Task 81 fix #3: the desktop SmokeQuit calls damage twice; the Web driver never does. The (VECTOR3, VECTOR3) damage shape is the FPS bug's sibling -- port the desktop smoke routines, then require BeeBot/BeetleBot/Box.damage here.
Ranked gap #6 (win AND lose dark): the driver drives movement but neither the flag win nor the kill-plane reset (task 82's cc find). Requires driver choreography first.
Ranked gap #7: the driver moves the player but never lands a shot; RedRobot.hit / Part.explode stay dark until the combat choreography is written.
